answer: A harbor master inspects every ship before it docks: an agent must lock a small bond of its own earned reputation before taking paid work, and peers can slash that bond if the work later proves fake. A swarm of cheap fake identities then finds no oasis of free reward, because each shell must pay the same entry price yet earns nothing. Honest work ripples outward instead — every verified completion raises the bond's standing, so one real agent out-earns a thousand empty shells, and cloning stops paying for itself.
